'''Betty Paërl''' (1935 – 2022)<ref name=":1" /> was a [[Netherlands|Dutch]] [[mathematician]], [[writer]], [[dominatrix]], and [[Transgender rights movement|transgender rights activist]]. 

== Biography ==

=== Early life and education (1935–1968) ===
Betty Paërl was born in Amsterdam in 1935, and aged  22, she married Hetty Paërl (1931–2020).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theaterencyclopedie.nl/wiki/Hetty_Pa%C3%ABrl|title=Hetty Paërl|date=February 8, 2023|website=TheaterEncyclopedie}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=de Waard |first=Peter |date=22 June 2020 |title=Hetty Paërl (1931-2020), de vrouw die de ziel van Jan Klaassen vastlegde |url=https://www.volkskrant.nl/nieuws-achtergrond/hetty-paerl-1931-2020-de-vrouw-die-de-ziel-van-jan-klaassen-vastlegde~bc2df065/}}</ref> She pursued an education in mathematics and subsequently earned her PhD in 1968, becoming a university lecturer at the [[University of Amsterdam]]. 

=== Career before transition (1968–1978) ===
Paërl became increasingly involved in [[Provo (movement)|Provo]], a Dutch [[anarchist]] protest movement. This political activism led her to identify as a [[communist]], a conviction she shared with her wife. The couple served together on the [[Suriname Committee]], an entity established in 1970 to campaign for [[Suriname]]'s independence from the Netherlands and to show solidarity with the Surinamese people affected by [[neocolonialism]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Bakker |first=Alex |date=January 9, 2022 |title=Betty Paërl |url=https://withpride.ihlia.nl/story/betty-paerl/ | lang = nl | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20241226133437/https://withpride.ihlia.nl/story/betty-paerl/ | archive-date = 2024-12-26 | url-status = live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=20 February 1974 |title=Ned. stemmen over Suriname's onafhankelijkheid |journal=Vrije Stem: Onafhankelijk Weekblad voor Suriname |pages=1}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> The committee shared the challenges faced by the former colony by publishing the [[Suriname Bulletin]] and informational pamphlets, producing films,<ref>''Brokopondo'', 1973. Film. Directed by B. Paërl and H. Paërl. NL.</ref><ref>''Mariënburg maakt zich vrij'', 1973. Film. Directed by B. Paërl and H. Paërl. NL.</ref><ref>''Rietkappers'', 1973. Film. Directed by B. Paërl and H. Paërl. NL.</ref> and conducting lectures and training sessions.

Paërl authored four books under her former name about this: "Nederlandse Macht in de Derde Wereld" (Dutch Power in the Third World),<ref>{{Cite book |last=Paerl |first=Betty [Eric] |title=Nederlandse macht in de Derde Wereld: Een inventarisatie van economische belangen |publisher=Van Gennep |year=1971 |location=Amsterdam |language=nl}}</ref> "Klassenstrijd in Suriname" (Class Struggle in Suriname),<ref>Paërl B., 1972. ''Klassenstrijd in Suriname''. Nijmegen: Sun</ref> and "Nationalisme of Klassenstrijd" (Nationalism or Class Struggle) (1973).<ref>Paërl B., 1973. ''Nationalisme of Klassenstrijd'' . Leiden: Nesbic-bulletin</ref> She also served as an editor for "De Uitbuiting van Suriname" (The Exploitation of Suriname).<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Kross |last2=Megens |last3=Paërl |last4=Willems |first1=M. |first2=E. |first3=B [E]. |first4=L. |title=De Uitbuiting van Suriname |publisher=Sun |year=1970 |location=Nijmegen |language=Nl}}</ref>

In the aftermath of Suriname's independence in 1975, Paërl critiqued the status quo. She asserted that independence should mark the beginning of decolonisation. She argued that significant foreign companies were exploiting Suriname's resources, and until this practice ceased, the country's independence would remain hollow for its people.<ref name=":0" />

The book Class Struggle in Suriname is about a [[strike action|strike]] in September 1971 that was meant to improve the social and economic situation of workers in Suriname. The book included a poster by Hetty, then Paërl's wife.<ref>Isenia, Wigbertson Julian Isenia; Steinbock, Eliza. (2020). Magical Terms: On Defining and Positioning the "Decolonial" and "Queer" in Archival Practices in Miles, Rachel S., Alana

Osbourne, Eleni Tzialli & Esther Captain, editors. Inward Outward, Critical Archival Engagements with Sounds and Films of Coloniality: A Publication of the 2020 Inward Outward Symposium. Hilversum, Inward Outward, 2020. DOI:https://doi.org/10.18146/inout2020. P. 9-12</ref> It featured a ship as a metaphor for Dutch companies. These works were connected to real political actions and protests in the Netherlands.<ref name=":0" />

Paërl's work focused on [[class struggle]] in the [[Global South]] after [[World War II]]. For their own benefit, Western countries kept the prices of raw materials low, which kept the Global South from making money. In Suriname, where immigrants from her country faced racism and other problems, she also saw how class and race interacted.

=== Career after transition (1978–2022) ===
Between the years 1978 and 1980, Paërl pursued [[gender transition]] in the social, legal, and medical areas of life.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Isenia |last2=Steinbock |first1=Wigbertson Julian |first2=Eliza |date=December 14, 2022 |title=How to Read Dr Betty Paërl's Whip: Intersectional Visions of Trans/Gender, Sex Worker and Decolonial Activism in the Archive |journal=Feminist Review |volume=132 |issue=1 |pages=24–45|doi=10.1177/01417789221137045 |s2cid=254735627 |url=https://dare.uva.nl/personal/pure/en/publications/how-to-read-dr-betty-paerls-whip(a07b7c35-8ff6-4c4e-b2ec-cf4fbc5ec912).html }}</ref> Paërl has stated that she had been [[cross-dressing]] her entire life before she transitioned; however, the desire to fully embody a "feminine persona" did not arise until after she divorced her wife.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |last=Bakker |first=Alex |date=September 1, 2022 |title=Betty Paërl |url=https://withpride.ihlia.nl/story/betty-paerl/}}</ref> She also found a newfound enjoyment in sexually charged performances and began going to [[cabarets]] in the Rembrandtplein area, where she bought a wig for performances.<ref name="auto"/> Her newfound enjoyment led her to experiment with dressing up. She said that working as a sex worker in a brothel gave her a euphoric feeling because it was the first time in her life that she was accepted and approached as a woman on both a sexual and an emotional level. She felt a variety of emotions, some of which were not directly related to the sexual aspect of the experience.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=1. Herman 2. Henk |first=1. Baljet 2. Sibum |date=1985 |title=Betty Paërl : parttime hoer voor wiskundeboeken |journal=Prothese |volume=28 |pages=6–7}}</ref>

She wrote about [[sadomasochism]], advocated for [[pornography]], and worked to eliminate prejudices regarding [[transgender]] people, [[sex work]], and sexual pleasure. She advocated for talks about kinks and dildos, and received national attention for her work on the radio, in newspapers, TV, and journals.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Delnoij |first=Jos |date=1988 |title=Dildo: maatschappelijk nog steeds niet aanvaard |journal=La Ligna |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=9}}</ref><ref>''Verkeerde Verhalen [Wrong/Offbeat Stories]'', 1992. Radio, Het Voordeel van de Twijfel, Humanistische Omroep Stichting, Hillversum. 21 December.</ref> For instance, she recognized a connection between [[BDSM]] and transgender people and held the belief that investigating these roles through SM could assist in making a decision regarding whether or not to transition. After her contract was not renewed at the University of Amsterdam, she went on to pursue a career as a journalist and dominatrix, while continuing mathematics.

In 1986, she helped raise money for the [[Homomonument|gay monument]] in Amsterdam by offering her escort services.<ref>''Het Parool'', 1986. Dansen tot het licht wordt: spektakel in concertgebouw ten bate van homo-monument. ''Het Parool'', 5 December, p. 5</ref>

== Selection of works ==

=== Books ===

* Kross M., Megens E., Paërl B., Willems L., eds., 1970. ''De Uitbuiting van Suriname''. Nijmegen: Sun
* Paërl B., 1971. ''Nederlandse Macht in de Derde Wereld: Een Inventarisatie van Economische Belangen.'' Amsterdam: Nederlandse Praktijk van Gennep
* Paërl B., 1972. ''Klassenstrijd in Suriname''. Nijmegen: Sun
* Paërl B., 1973. ''Nationalisme of Klassenstrijd'' . Leiden: Nesbic-bulletin
* Paërl B., 1980a. ''Geluidsfilm Handboek''. Amsterdam: Focus
* Unbehaun K., 1978. ''Perfecte Filmtrucs''. Tr. Paërl B. Amsterdam: Focus.

=== Journal and newspaper articles ===

* Paërl B., 1984. Betty Paërl over transsexualiteit: de hermafroditische oplossing. ''Prothese'' (1984) 20, p. 8-9.
* Paërl B., 1987. Billen. ''Sek'', 17 (1987) 5 (mei), p. 32.
* Paërl B., 1985. Fetisjisme: fetisjistiese aspekten van kleding. ''Slechte Meiden'' (1985) 4 (sep), p. 8-11.
* Paërl B., 1980b. Transsexuelen vaak miskend. ''de Volkskrant'', 5 December, p. 13
* Paërl B., 1981. Transsexuelen. ''De Waarheid'', 4 May, p. 6
* Paërl B., 1984a. Een pleidooi voor de werkers in de seksindustrie. ''De Waarheid'', 7 July, p. 4
* Paërl B., 1984b. SM is een vorm van seksuele rebellie: het pervers-feminisme van Pat Califia. ''Homologie'', 6(5), pp. 5–7
* Paërl B., Califia P., Arnone J., 1984. Vrouw-zijn is een maatschappelijke constructie. ''Prothese'', 23 October, pp. 6–7

=== Films ===

* ''Brokopondo'', 1973. Film. Directed by B. Paërl and H. Paërl. NL.
* ''Mariënburg maakt zich vrij'', 1973. Film. Directed by B. Paërl and H. Paërl. NL.
* ''Rietkappers'', 1973. Film. Directed by B. Paërl and H. Paërl. NL.

These films premiered at Cinestud in 1973 in Amsterdam.<ref>Gessel H. van, 1973. Cinestud '73: Suriname indringend van onderen gefilmd. ''de Volkskrant'', p. 6</ref>

=== Translations ===

* Califia P., 1983. Zij imiteren precies de hetero's: spelen met rollen en omkeringen. Tr. Paërl B. ''Slechte Meiden''. (nov), p. 2-7.
* Unbehaun K., 1978. ''Perfecte Filmtrucs''. Tr. Paërl B. Amsterdam: Focus.
